name: Erik Ibrahim

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I’m with the independent Work Futures Panel. We have no ties to employers, AI firms, unions or government, and we keep your answers confidential. What is a normal workday for you?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I’m 43, have a bachelor’s degree, and have managed the customer move-in accounts team at a large utility company for nine years. Seven clerks report to me. We open new accounts, sort bills when a meter number is wrong, and make sure a family moving house does not pay for the last occupant’s power. I know the ordinary rules, though our specialist checks the difficult commercial contracts. I have never used an AI tool.

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: My wife works in a florist’s shop, and our children are eleven and sixteen. We have a mortgage and about four months of expenses saved. My pay is ordinary for a manager, with some similar jobs nearby. I like the work to be done properly, and I do not put much faith in a tool nobody can explain.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. "Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d tell the team AI Plateau sounds like another filing aid. A family still needs a person to look at the meter photograph before a first bill is sent.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think my job and pay remain safe with such a small change. The mortgage matters, but four months saved and my wife’s wage give us breathing space. I would watch the florist’s slow winter more closely than the office tool.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I’d keep the two-clerk check on a disputed first bill. If a new sorting system comes in, I’d ask our billing specialist to show me five rejected accounts before I approve its use; I will not run it myself just to look keen. We would keep our monthly savings transfer while both wages arrive.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel uneasy because winter shop hours can fall. My office job looks safe in the AI Plateau picture, but the mortgage still comes each month.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Which photograph matters?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Last week a new tenant sent a picture of the meter with the serial number clear. Our move-in file had the old meter listed, and the first bill would have charged the wrong flat. A clerk caught the mismatch before posting it.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why ask the specialist rather than try the sorter?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: She has seen more billing errors than I have, and I would trust her record of what the software missed. I learn a new system once it has proved useful. I have not used AI myself and do not intend to be first for a meeting.

say: **AI Plateau** may sort files, but clerks still check meter photographs.
A first bill needs the **right meter number** before posting.
think: My own **job and pay** look secure under a small tool change.
The florist’s **winter hours** still matter to our mortgage budget.
do: **Keep** two-clerk checks on disputed first bills in 2026.
**Inspect** five rejected accounts with the billing specialist before approving a sorter.
**Continue** monthly savings transfers while both wages arrive.
feel: I feel **uneasy** about winter shop hours, though my office job looks safe.
S0.quote: Our move-in file had the old meter listed, and the first bill would have charged the wrong flat.
fieldNote: His **four-month reserve** makes routine AI manageable, while a seasonal household wage keeps him watchful.
He has **never used AI** and asks an experienced specialist to demonstrate real failures first.
He says **uneasy**, but winter florist hours could shrink household income while the mortgage stays due.

steps.text: Keep two clerks checking disputed first bills against meter photographs
Continue monthly savings transfer while both household wages arrive

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. "Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say Steady Disruption could write account letters, check meter files, book visits and answer easy questions. I would ask management to show us the error reports before reducing the clerks.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately, most of our day is exactly that screen work. I have nine years’ experience, but two account teams could be put together and one manager post removed. Our savings buy a few months, not a replacement for my wage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I’d list the corrected meter errors our clerks find and take them to the monthly operations meeting. If the new software is approved, I’d attend a paid demonstration with our billing specialist and practise only after its mistakes are clear. If our team shrinks, I’d check the posted field-service coordinator role, but apply only if its salary and hours cover our mortgage and the eleven-year-old’s school pickup. I would accept a small pay cut only after a real offer and rota, and only if my wife’s steady florist hours kept the mortgage covered.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious. I would rather face the real numbers than call myself safe because I have worked here a long time.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What mistake should go in that list?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A landlord submitted the same meter photograph for two flats. The billing software could mark both meter forms complete, but a clerk noticed the identical serial number. I would show the cost of reversing the wrong bills.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you take a pay cut for field service?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A small cut might work if my wife’s hours are steady, but I need the actual offer and rota. I would not trade our mortgage payment for a promise of more work later. My wife and I would do the sums together.

say: **Account automation** needs published meter-error figures before staff cuts.
I’d show the **cost of wrong bills**, not just processing speed.
think: A merged office could remove **one manager post**, including mine.
Four months saved cannot replace my **wage** for long.
do: **Attend** a paid demonstration, then practise approved software only after its mistakes are clear.
**Apply** for the posted field role only if listed salary covers mortgage and hours fit school pickup.
**Accept** a small pay cut only after a real offer, rota and steady florist hours keep the mortgage covered.
feel: I feel **anxious** about a possible merged manager post.
S1.quote: The billing software could mark both meter forms complete, but a clerk noticed the identical serial number.
fieldNote: He uses **real meter errors** to argue for people before headcount changes.
His possible **field move** needs an actual offer, mortgage pay and school-compatible hours.

steps.text: Record duplicate meter errors found by clerks for monthly meeting
Attend paid demo and practise approved billing software only after specialist explains errors
Apply for posted field role only if listed pay covers mortgage and hours fit school pickup
Accept lower-paid field offer only if rota and steady florist wages keep mortgage covered

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. "Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d tell the office AGI by 2028 could write bills, check accounts and answer customers without our desk. I would ask for a date on any cut and a named person to hear a wrong-bill appeal.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Full thinking AI in 2028 could do nearly all my office work. Robots that can do hands-on meter visits arrive around 2031, but the field coordinator’s planning and reports face AGI in 2028 too. I expect the account team to shrink, and my manager job might go.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Tomorrow I’d ask the operations director for written notice and severance figures. I’d phone two nearby utilities about posted field coordinator jobs only if the pay after travel covers the mortgage and the rota lets an adult collect our younger child. If AGI arrives in 2028 and I lose my post, I’d use the four-month reserve for bills while I take a confirmed offer, not assume a vacancy is waiting.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious and I can hear the mortgage date in my head. I have a plan and some local firms to call, but four months would pass quickly.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you ask about the field role?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Who checks the actual meter, who writes the report and what hours the coordinator works. Field-service reports are not safe from AGI just because a technician visits the meter. A site visit is useful only if there is paid work attached.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you say to your wife?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would say the office may be cut, and we should not put the reserve into a holiday. She knows the florist’s winter can be slow. We would keep the children’s school routine until an offer changed it.

say: **AGI by 2028** needs cut dates and a human appeal for wrong bills.
I would ask for **severance figures** before any decision.
think: Office and field reports face **2028 AGI**, before meter-visit robots around 2031.
My manager post might go, with **four months saved** to search.
do: **Ask** the director tomorrow for written notice and severance figures.
**Contact** two utilities only for field jobs with mortgage pay after travel and workable pickup hours.
**Use** the reserve for bills after a cut while taking a confirmed offer.
feel: I feel **anxious** about losing my post, with a short but real cushion.
S2.quote: Field-service reports are not safe from AGI just because a technician visits the meter.
fieldNote: He distinguishes **2028 desk risk** from physical meter visits changed by robots around 2031.
The **reserve and local firms** give a short search, not a guaranteed new job.

steps.text: Call utilities only for field jobs with mortgage-covering pay after travel and school-compatible hours

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. "Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say AGI by 2031 gives us five years to sort out which account disputes still need a person. I would rather learn a proven field process than buy a course on a guess.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My billing desk could still go in 2031, and field coordination has screen planning exposed then too. Robots able to inspect meters arrive around 2034, so hands-on visits change later. I have some local options, but I cannot count a vacancy before seeing one.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: From January 2027 I’d take a paid week with the field team only if my director arranges cover for the account desk and protects my salary. I’d ask a technician to show me how a meter serial number is checked on site. After AGI arrives in 2031, I’d apply for a coordinator vacancy only if the posted pay after travel and the rota cover our mortgage and family hours.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about the office job. Five years would let me try field work without leaving wages behind.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you do on the paid week?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Walk into two buildings with a technician and compare the meter against our account file. I know the billing paperwork, not the meter wiring or access rules. I would ask the technician to correct my notes before I used them.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if the director refuses cover?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep managing the desk and ask for a single paid site day later. I will not leave seven clerks without someone to approve a disputed bill. My wife and I need my current pay while I test this.

say: **Five years** allows a paid field test before a job switch.
I would check **serial numbers on site** with a technician.
think: Billing and field planning face **2031 AGI**, before meter robots around 2034.
A **local vacancy** may not be open when I need it.
do: **Take** a paid field week from January 2027 only with desk cover and full salary.
**Learn** meter checks from a technician during that approved week.
**Apply** after 2031 only if posted pay after travel and family rota cover mortgage.
feel: I feel **anxious** about desk loss, with time for a paid field test.
S3.quote: I know the billing paperwork, not the meter wiring or access rules.
fieldNote: He accepts a **bounded field trial** only with desk cover and protected wages.
His **field fallback** still has planning exposed to AGI in 2031, before physical robots arrive.

steps.text: Take paid field week only with account-desk cover and full salary
Learn on-site meter checks from technician during approved paid week
Apply after 2031 for posted coordinator job only if net pay covers mortgage and rota works

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. "Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say AGI by 2036 gives firms time to publish real field jobs and the pay attached to them. I would ask for a clear route from the account desk before anyone is told to retrain.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Our younger child will be about twenty-one in 2036 and the older one about twenty-six. If both wages hold, we might have cut the mortgage and built more savings. My account and field planning work still faces thinking AI in 2036, while hands-on meter robots come around 2039. I would not treat a long runway as a reason to quit a steady job now.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I’d keep the two-clerk bill check and continue the monthly savings transfer while both wages arrive. I’d review posted field coordinator roles each spring, and take a paid site posting only if the salary covers our mortgage and the work includes real meter visits. After AGI arrives in 2036, I’d stay only while the field post still has paid work and bills are covered.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel uneasy. Ten years gives the family room, though I would want the company to be honest about what field work remains.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you move house for the role?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Not on a possible vacancy. Our mortgage is manageable now and the children know this area. In 2036 they will be adults, so my wife and I could reconsider then if a real offer made the move sensible.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would make a site posting real?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A wage figure, a rota and actual meter visits rather than another desk full of automated reports. I would ask to speak to a technician about the work. I can learn field work, but I want to see an actual meter-visit job first.

say: A **decade** should bring posted field jobs with wages attached.
I would ask for **real meter visits**, not another screen title.
think: Two wages could reduce the **mortgage** and grow savings by 2036.
Account and field planning face **2036 AGI**, before meter robots around 2039.
do: **Keep** two-clerk bill checks and savings transfers in 2026.
**Review** posted field coordinator roles each spring.
**Take** a paid site posting only with mortgage pay and meter visits; after 2036 stay only while work and bills remain covered.
feel: I feel **uneasy** about later field work despite time to choose.
S4.quote: I can learn field work, but I want to see an actual meter-visit job first.
fieldNote: His **ten-year horizon** changes the children’s ages and leaves any future move conditional on a real offer.
He asks for **wages and visits** before trading a known desk for a title.

steps.text: Keep two clerks checking disputed first bills through 2026
Continue monthly savings transfers while both wages arrive
Take posted field role only if salary covers mortgage and includes meter visits
Stay in field role after 2036 only with paid work covering household bills

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because the account desk could shrink before I know whether field jobs will pay enough. A cut date, severance figures and a paid field week would help me judge. Four months saved buys a search, not a new wage.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn’t ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: Ask the family who receives a first bill for a meter they do not own. An account can look tidy on the screen and still charge the wrong flat. Someone has to check the photograph.

headlineQuote: An account can look tidy on the screen and still charge the wrong flat.
portrait: **Erik, 43**, is an experienced move-in accounts manager at a large utility company with a bachelor’s degree.
His **typical pay**, florist wife, four-month reserve and some nearby jobs support a mortgage and two school-age children.
He has **never used AI**, checks meter photographs and asks specialists to demonstrate failures before trusting new systems.
He is **anxious** about winter household pay even in AI Plateau, then explores field work under wage and rota conditions.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could shrink his account desk before a field job with adequate pay appears.
whatWouldHelp: A written **cut date**, severance figures and a paid field week would help him judge.
